reference_note: golden/expected.bin is an independent numpy float32 forward pass over the stored fp16 weights/inputs/tables; it shares no code with the flatbuffer writer (which contains no maths).  A float64 rerun gives 7140/7168 identical fp16 codes (max|f32-f64| = 1.212e-04), so the reference is not precision-limited.
tolerance_basis: max|out| = 0.4836; fp16 ULP at that magnitude = 0.0002441 (5.05e-04 relative). Device-independent floor (numpy chain with a fp16 rounding at every tensor boundary, i.e. what MDLA does -- docs/OP-qkv.md 5.2: 7167/7168 bit-identical) = 4.8828e-04 abs = 2.00 ULP = 1.01e-03 relative. Registered atol = rtol = max(4*2^-11*max|out|, 4*floor) = 0.00195312. The 4*floor term dominates. NOTES 4's flat 2e-2 would be 4.14e-02 relative here, i.e. looser than the measured floor (usable but weak).
tolerance_revision: registered before the first board run of this op; derived only from the frozen fixture + a device-independent fp16 rounding simulation (NOTES 4 / 10.1).  Not adjusted after any run.

fp16_floor.note: numpy chain with a fp16 rounding at every tensor boundary vs the single-rounding golden; device-independent

eps_register.note: Qwen2.5 rms_norm_eps = 1e-6 (transformers), NOT the earlier toy block's 0 (docs/OP-block.md).  The mean(x^2) of a real hidden is ~1e-4..1, so eps moves the output by << 1 ULP: the two conventions are numerically indistinguishable here and are NOT discriminated by this comparison.  The graph carries the real 1e-6 anyway (it is what the model means).
